clue.text: Part of abolitionist that is corrupt, but whose spirit is pure and free

definitions.text: Part of abolitionist that is corrupt, but whose spirit is pure and free

parts.words: Part of abolitionist that is corrupt, but whose spirit is pure and free
parts.note: the Civil War marching song says the abolitionist's corpse lies mouldering in the grave while his soul goes marching on

explanation.surface: A riddle about a slavery campaigner whose flesh decays while his soul stays untainted.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotting remains of the hanged abolitionist are the subject of the famous American song whose refrain says his soul marches on.

clue.text: Mad to undo dam-not quite one of the party, as it were!

definitions.text: not quite one of the party, as it were

indicators.note: something mad is crazed or deranged, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone frantically trying to dismantle a dam is plainly not fitting in with the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like part of the picture but signals that TO UNDO DAM is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit who does not belong with the rest of a group is the classic phrase for the one left over.

clue.text: Goad? Yes, but smaller

parts.note: a goad is a long pointed stick for driving cattle; a sharp sewing implement is a much smaller pointed thing, and to goad is also to provoke or annoy

explanation.surface: A question-and-answer exchange about a prod being scaled down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to provoke someone, a sense of goad, and literally names a tiny pointed tool.

clue.text: Lock part of a guardian's responsibility

definitions.meaning: a ridge inside a lock that only the right key can pass
a minor placed under the care of a legal guardian

explanation.surface: Part of a padlock described as something a guardian must look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a notched lock component and a child under legal protection share this word.

clue.text: Drink to Fleet Street being put down!

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
Fleet Street in London was the home of British newspapers, so it stands for the press

explanation.surface: A drinker toasts the newspaper world as it is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: FLEET STREET was the London home of the national newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash or crush a rebellion or a story is to put it down.

clue.text: Well, one would expect to find it in the desert

definitions.text: Well, one would expect to find it in the desert

parts.words: Well, one would expect to find it in the desert
parts.note: 'Well' reads as a casual opener but is the thing itself: a fertile spot with water in a desert

explanation.surface: A speaker musing on what turns up in arid places.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering place with vegetation amid sand is exactly what a desert well provides.

clue.text: Points to theologian returning to America. Quick, isn't it?

indicators.note: returning means the run of points, theologian and America is read backwards

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A divine heads back to the States in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the whole run NE+DD+US, giving the answer backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrupt and unexpected happens quickly, without warning.

clue.text: Ill received grant of time off?

definitions.text: Ill received grant of time off?

parts.words: Ill received grant of time off?
parts.note: read as 'badly received permission' it sounds ungrateful, but it means an absence granted because one is unwell

explanation.surface: Someone resents being given a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence from work allowed on grounds of illness is the familiar employment term.

clue.text: One offering to give a ring to his insurance broker?

definitions.text: One offering to give a ring to his insurance broker?

parts.words: One offering to give a ring to his insurance broker?
parts.note: a man offering a ring asks for marriage, and the person applying for insurance cover is also so called

explanation.surface: A suitor who phones the man who sells him policies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the suitor asking for a hand in marriage and the applicant filling in an insurance form go by this title.

clue.text: Burnt by the church that'll infuriate people!

definitions.meaning: an aromatic resin set smouldering in religious services

explanation.surface: Something the church burns that will enrage the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is fragrant gum burnt in worship; the verb means to anger greatly.

clue.text: Hold on to something uncooked in a hideously servile manner

indicators.note: in places the uncooked thing inside the word for holding on

parts.note: to grip or clutch something tightly is to cling
raw food is uncooked

explanation.surface: Clutching raw food in a grovelling way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawning, abject flattery is described as creeping or crawling behaviour.

clue.text: Runs hands over body, trying to find arms, perhaps

definitions.text: Runs hands over body, trying to find arms, perhaps

parts.words: Runs hands over body, trying to find arms, perhaps
parts.note: a police search for concealed weapons, where 'arms' tempts one to think of limbs

explanation.surface: Someone feeling about a body looking for its limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Police search a suspect by patting them down for hidden weapons.

clue.text: One lying back while others are marching?

definitions.text: One lying back while others are marching?

parts.words: One lying back while others are marching?
parts.note: 'lying back' suggests reclining but means trailing behind the column

explanation.surface: A lazy soldier lounging while the troops march.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lags behind the main body of a march falls behind the rest.

clue.text: Jumped off!

parts.note: it means both jumped in surprise and began, as in set off

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone leapt down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both flinched with a jolt and set out or began.

clue.text: Steal back a hammer, for instance

indicators.note: back means the word for the hammer's category is read in reverse

parts.note: a hammer is an example of a tool

explanation.surface: Someone pinching a hammer back.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder or pillage is to steal goods.

clue.text: Printed part of the book

parts.note: the main body of printed words in a book, as distinct from illustrations or margins

explanation.surface: A description of a page's contents.
explanation.definitionFit: The written words forming the body of a book or document are its wording.

clue.text: A hundred-eyed one chewing up sweet

indicators.note: chewing something up mangles it, so the giant's name is rearranged

parts.note: Argus was the giant of Greek myth with a hundred eyes

explanation.surface: A many-eyed monster munching a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Argus is the hundred-eyed watchman of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet as a noun can mean a sweetener, and a term of endearment, both senses this word carries.

clue.text: Fighter is happy I changed rota

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: changed means the letters of rota are rearranged

explanation.surface: A combatant pleased that the duty roster was altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena combatant is a classic fighter.

clue.text: Does he get a rake-off from the casino?

definitions.text: Does he get a rake-off from the casino?

parts.words: Does he get a rake-off from the casino?
parts.note: a rake-off is a cut of the profits, but the gaming-table attendant literally uses a rake to gather chips

explanation.surface: A question about who takes a skim of casino money.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino employee who runs the table gathers stakes with a rake.

clue.text: Stage one in theatrical production

parts.note: 'Stage one' sounds like a first step but means a person of the stage, one who performs in a play

explanation.surface: The first phase of putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in a play is a person of the stage.

clue.text: Knight bearing a monarch's name

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir, and a king is formally addressed by a longer form of that title

explanation.surface: A knight named after a king.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic mode of address for a sovereign extends the knight's honorific by one letter.

clue.text: Criminal group to go for the Scots

definitions.meaning: in Scots dialect the verb means to go

explanation.surface: A crime ring heading north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots verb for go is gang, as in Burns's 'gang aft agley'.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of crooks is a mob, and in Scottish dialect the same word means to walk or go.

clue.text: The greater part of the French is held to interfere with one

indicators.note: is held means the French article sits inside the word for the greater part

parts.note: most means the greater part
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Most of the French are said to be meddling with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or harass someone is to interfere with them.

clue.text: Good, book second place in departure en masse

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Good Book, the Bible

explanation.surface: A stylish volume and a mass exodus of people, read as one sentence about a ranking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's second book recounts the Israelites leaving Egypt, and the word now means any mass departure.

clue.text: A wise old bird? No-young

parts.note: the proverbially wise bird, but a baby one rather than an old one

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a description of a sage elder.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby of the bird thought wise is a chick of that night hunter.

clue.text: Late for Divine service? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: Late for Divine service? Quite the reverse

parts.words: Late for Divine service? Quite the reverse
parts.note: 'Late' means dead: this is a church service for the deceased, not someone tardy

explanation.surface: Someone running late for church, or perhaps not.
explanation.definitionFit: A service held in honour of the dead commemorates them.

clue.text: Proverbially, one nagged for nothing should skip this examination!

definitions.text: Proverbially, one nagged for nothing should skip this examination!

parts.words: Proverbially, one nagged for nothing should skip this examination!
parts.note: the spoken test, avoided by someone who is told off over nothing and keeps his mouth shut

explanation.surface: Advice that a henpecked person should miss a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A test conducted by speaking rather than writing is a viva or spoken examination.

clue.text: They provide coal for ships

parts.note: both coal miners and the ships that carry coal share this name

explanation.surface: A description of the suppliers who fuel steamships.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners dig coal and coal-carrying vessels bear the same name.

clue.text: Superior to a gambler?

explanation.surface: Being above a gambler in standing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of good and a person who places wagers.

clue.text: Our shy Latin art is changed, there's science for you!

indicators.note: is changed means the letters of the preceding four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy Latin art is altered, and there you have science.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of plants, animals and the natural world is a branch of science.
